- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon when sentiment is high (e.g., >0.6) — model tends to overreact to bullish sentiment.
- Underestimate when sentiment is low (e.g., <0.4) — model misses downward momentum or fails to anticipate sharp drops.
- Overshoot after recent spikes — model often peaks too early and then underperforms, especially if sentiment was high before the spike.
- Mean-reversion bias: model tends to overcorrect after strong moves, especially in the 10–15 day window.
- Lagged response to sentiment: model reacts to sentiment shifts with a 2–3 day delay, so if sentiment rises sharply, forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–2 days.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are consistently too low in the first 5–7 days, then rise toward true values — model underestimates early momentum.
- Avoid “flat” forecasts when sentiment is volatile — model tends to ignore sentiment swings and produces overly conservative outputs.
